title: Your first video in 15 minutes
summary: Pick a format, write a hook that lands in two seconds, film once, check the score.

blocks.body: You do not need a studio, a ring light or a following. You need a brief, one format and a first line that earns the next ten seconds. The Studio walks you through all three, and this lesson explains the thinking so you can do it without the prompts.

blocks.title: Why the first three seconds decide it
blocks.body: Viewers decide inside two or three seconds whether to keep watching. The Hook Score is a checklist built from what winning app videos have in common: the hook line lands by 2.0 seconds, the same words appear on screen within a second, a face or a screen is in frame, and the app is visible by 0:03. Each item is worth points, and each has a one-tap fix.

blocks.title: The 15 minutes
blocks.body:
Read the brief TL;DR (2 min)
Pick a format and a hook (3 min)
Film once, one take, phone upright (5 min)
Check the Hook Score and fix the top item (3 min)
Submit (2 min)

blocks.title: Choosing a hook
blocks.body: Seven hook types work for app videos. A confession ("I was wrong about every workout app I tried before Stridely") disarms cold viewers. A specific number ("Seven minutes a day, seven days") signals honesty. A question names a pain the viewer already has. A POV puts them in the scene. Risk reversal ("free for seven days, cancel in two taps") lowers the cost of trying. Pick the one you can say naturally in one breath.

blocks.title: Fix a slow opening
blocks.body: Before: "Hi guys, today I want to show you an app I have been using." After: "I was wrong about editing apps." The second line is the hook; the first is a warm-up. Cut the warm-up and start on the line you would have said at second four.

blocks.title: One sentence, three checks
blocks.body: "I was wrong about every workout app I tried before Stridely." Spoken in 1.6 seconds, the same words on screen at 0:00, the app on screen by 0:03. That one sentence passes the timing check, the text-match check and the app-visible check.

blocks.title: Pre-flight in 30 seconds
blocks.body:
Hook lands by 2 seconds
Same words on screen as text
App visible by 3 seconds
#ad spoken and shown
One call to action, then stop

blocks.title: Common slip
blocks.body: A slow intro, or reading the hook off a script with your eyes down. Look at the lens for the first line, and if the first three seconds are setup, cut them.

blocks.title: After you submit
blocks.body: The brand decides within 72 hours. A yes gives you your link, code and #ad line. A request for changes comes with timecoded notes, and two revision rounds are included. A no always carries a reason code and evidence, and you can appeal once.

quiz.prompt: By when should your hook land?
quiz.explanation: The Hook Score gives full points when the hook lands by 2.0 seconds.

quiz.prompt: Where should the spoken hook also appear?
options: On screen as text within a second
quiz.explanation: Matching on-screen text within the first second keeps viewers who watch on mute.

quiz.prompt: When should the app appear?
quiz.explanation: The app must be visible early, not only at the end.

title: Reading a brief and a Rights Card
summary: What you must say, what you must not, and what the brand may do with your video.

blocks.body: Every bounty has a brief (what to make) and a Rights Card (what the brand may do with it). Read both before you film. It takes two minutes and prevents most rejections and most regrets.

blocks.title: The brief: what must be in the video
blocks.body: A brief lists required beats (the must-say and must-show list), do and do-not lists, one call to action, banned claims, the disclosure wording and the offer line. Required beats are checked automatically before your video reaches a person, so a missing beat comes back in minutes, not days. The do-not list matters as much: showing a competing app, using chart music or making a result claim are all common reasons for a no.

blocks.title: What to check on the Rights Card
blocks.body:
Required beats (the must-say list)
The do and do-not list
One call to action
Rights Card: organic is always included
Paid-ad usage: how many days, and the renewal price
AI likeness: off unless you agree separately

blocks.title: Reading the card
blocks.body: Paid ads: 90 days. Renewal: 25% of the base fee per 30 days. AI likeness: off. In plain English: the brand may run your video as an ad on TikTok and Meta for 90 days from approval, you approve each Spark code or partnership request, extending it costs the brand 25% of your base fee for every extra 30 days, and nobody may clone your face or voice.

blocks.title: Organic is always yours
blocks.body: Posting on your own account is always included. Paid ads are extra, have a term, and are priced up front.

blocks.title: Before you film: three questions
blocks.body: Can I say the must-say lines in my own words? Do I have a real moment of using the app to show? Does anything on the do-not list describe my usual style? If the answer to the last one is yes, ask in the bounty chat before you film. A two-line question now is cheaper than a re-shoot.

blocks.title: Plain-English Rights Card
blocks.body: Organic posting on your own account: always. Paid ads on TikTok and Meta: 90 days from approval. Renewal: 25% of your base fee per extra 30 days. AI likeness: off. If any line is missing, ask in the bounty chat before you film.

blocks.title: Perpetual rights
blocks.body: A Rights Card never says "forever". If a brief does, report it. Report any request for AI likeness inside a brief too: it is off unless you agree separately.

quiz.prompt: What is always included in a Rights Card?
options: Organic posting on your own account
Use of your face by AI
quiz.explanation: Organic posting is always included; everything else is explicit and time-limited.

quiz.prompt: What is the default paid-ad term?
quiz.explanation: The default is 90 days, renewable at 25% of the base fee per 30 days.

quiz.prompt: Is AI likeness included by default?
options: No, it is off by default
quiz.explanation: AI likeness needs separate, explicit consent.

title: Usage rights and what to charge
summary: Whitelisting, Spark codes, partnership ads, renewals, and how paid usage changes the price.

blocks.body: When a brand runs your video as an ad, it is using your content to sell. That is worth more than an organic post, so it is priced separately and it always has an end date.

blocks.title: The words
blocks.body:
Whitelisting: the ad runs from your handle
Spark code (TikTok): a code that lets a brand boost your post
Partnership permission (Meta): lets a brand run your post as an ad
Usage term: how long
Renewal: priced up front

blocks.title: How paid usage works here
blocks.body: The brand asks for permission on the post. You see who is asking, which platform, the term and the renewal price, and you accept or decline each request. Spark codes last 7, 30, 60 or 365 days and carry their own expiry. When the term on your Rights Card ends, the ad stops automatically, and the brand is alerted 30, 14 and 7 days before so there is time to renew or let it go.

blocks.title: What a renewal looks like
blocks.body: You were paid $120 for a video with 90 days of paid usage. On day 80 the brand asks to extend by 30 days. Renewal = 25% of $120 = $30, paid to you, priced up front on the card. No negotiation needed, and you can decline.

blocks.title: Pricing paid usage
blocks.body: Think of two prices: the fee for the video and the fee for the ad rights. Organic posting comes with the fee. Paid usage has a term and a renewal price. A common starting point is the video price for a 90-day term, with renewal at 25% of that price per extra 30 days.

blocks.title: Keep your own copy of the term
blocks.body: The Rights Vault shows every video that runs as an ad, who runs it, and when it ends. Check it monthly, and set your own reminder for any 365-day Spark code.

blocks.title: Ask about the end date
blocks.body: Ads should stop when your rights end. flowd stops them automatically and alerts at 30, 14 and 7 days. If you see an ad running past its date, open a rights dispute from the post.

blocks.title: AI likeness is separate
blocks.body: A synthetic copy of your face or voice is off on every Rights Card by default. It would be a separate agreement with its own price, and you can say no.

quiz.prompt: A Spark code lets a brand...
options: Boost your post as an ad
quiz.explanation: A Spark code authorises ads from your post; it has its own expiry.

quiz.prompt: Renewal is priced at...
options: 25% of the base fee per 30 days
quiz.explanation: Renewals are priced up front on the Rights Card.

quiz.prompt: When do ads stop?
quiz.explanation: Ads stop automatically at the end of the term.

title: Contract red flags
summary: Perpetual rights, pay-to-join, burner accounts, unpaid trials and view-minimum bases.

blocks.body: Most bad deals have the same few traps. Learn them and you will spot them in seconds.

blocks.title: The red flags
blocks.body:
Perpetual or unlimited usage
Pay to join or a deposit
A new account just for the brand
Unpaid test videos
Base pay only after a view minimum
Being asked to move to WhatsApp or Telegram

blocks.title: Why each one is a problem
blocks.body: Perpetual usage means a brand keeps selling with your face forever for the price of one video. A pay-to-join fee is the oldest scam there is: real brands pay creators, never the other way round. A burner account hides your audience from the work and puts the account at risk if the brand walks away. Unpaid trials ask for free work "to see if you fit". Base pay that only starts after a view minimum means you can do everything right and earn nothing. Moving to WhatsApp or Telegram removes escrow, the record of what was agreed and the report button.

blocks.title: Brief Lint blocks most of these
blocks.body: flowd blocks briefs that contain unpaid trials, view-minimum bases or burner-account demands. If you still see one, report it.

blocks.title: Safe version of a risky clause
blocks.body: Risky: "Creator grants brand all rights in perpetuity." Safe: "Creator grants 90 days of paid-ad usage; renewals priced at 25% of the base fee per 30 days." If you only see the risky version, report the brief.

blocks.title: A real trap
blocks.body: "Pay $25 to unlock the bounty and we will refund you after your first payout." Never. Real bounties are funded before they go live; a fee to join is the whole scam.

blocks.title: Keep it in the app
blocks.body: In-app chat only. flowd never asks you to pay and never asks you to move off the platform.

blocks.title: If something feels off
blocks.body:
Do not reply outside flowd
Screenshot the message
Tap Report on the bounty or message
Keep working only on Funded bounties

quiz.prompt: A brand asks for $25 to join. You should...
quiz.explanation: Real bounties never ask creators to pay.

quiz.prompt: A new account just for the brand is...
options: Not allowed in a flowd bounty
quiz.explanation: Bounties may not require burner or fresh accounts.

quiz.prompt: "Move to Telegram to finalise"
quiz.explanation: flowd never asks you to leave the app.

title: Platform rules and #ad
summary: Originality, reposts, watermarks and how to disclose properly.

blocks.body: TikTok and Instagram penalise unoriginal content, and the FTC expects clear disclosure when you are paid. Both are easy to get right once they are a habit.

blocks.title: Disclosure checklist
blocks.body:
Say it out loud ("this is a paid partnership with the app")
Show #ad on screen for 2 seconds
Put #ad at the start of the caption
Turn on the platform paid-partnership label

blocks.title: Why four places
blocks.body: Clear means easy to notice. Many viewers never open the caption, so the disclosure is spoken and shown in the video itself. The platform label is a separate setting that platforms check. flowd audits every post for the spoken line, the on-screen tag, the caption, the label, the music licence, banned claims, the AI label and your tracking link. A failed check holds the post's pay until you fix the caption or the brand waives it, so a quick fix is worth money.

blocks.title: A disclosure that works
blocks.body: Spoken in the first 5 seconds: "This is a paid partnership with Lumi." On screen: #ad for two full seconds, top-left, away from the caption bar. Caption starts with: "#ad Paid partnership with Lumi. Watch the glow-up."

blocks.title: Originality and music
blocks.body: Platforms push down reposted and unoriginal content, and brands cannot run videos with chart music as ads. Use your own footage and recordings, original audio, or a track from the commercial library. Do not reuse another creator's clip, even with credit, and do not post the same video on several accounts.

blocks.title: flowd adds it for you
blocks.body: Studio and the post screen add #ad and the brand wording and lock them so they cannot be forgotten. Turn on the paid-partnership label yourself when you post: it is separate from your caption.

blocks.title: Originality
blocks.body: Duplicate detection protects you as well: it compares every submission with the rest of the bounty and with your own history, so a recycled clip is caught before it can cost you a strike.

quiz.prompt: Where must #ad appear?
options: Spoken, on screen and in the caption
Nowhere if it is a review
quiz.explanation: Disclosure belongs in the video itself, not only in the caption.

quiz.prompt: Reposting the same video on many accounts can...
quiz.explanation: Low-originality reposts are penalised.

quiz.prompt: Who adds the disclosure text in flowd?
quiz.explanation: Auto-disclosure is locked in the post flow.

title: Taxes: W-9 and 1099
summary: When flowd asks for a W-9, what a 1099-NEC is and how to set money aside. Not tax advice.

blocks.body: You are paid as an independent creator, so you are responsible for your own taxes. flowd asks for a W-9 when your first video is approved, before your first payout. This is general information, not tax advice.

blocks.title: What happens
blocks.body:
First approval: we ask for a W-9
Year to date: shown in Tax Desk
$2,000 or more paid in 2026: US creators receive a 1099-NEC
Set-aside estimate: 25% by default, adjustable

blocks.title: W-9 or W-8BEN
blocks.body: US creators fill in a W-9: legal name, address and taxpayer ID. Creators outside the US fill in a W-8BEN, which says where you are a tax resident. The app only ever shows the last four digits of a taxpayer ID. Until the form is verified your earnings still clear, but the payout waits, so do it the day it is asked for.

blocks.title: What a 1099-NEC is
blocks.body: It is a form that reports payments to independent contractors. For payments made in 2026 the threshold is $2,000: if flowd pays a US creator $2,000 or more in the year, a 1099-NEC is issued in January 2027. Below the line you still owe tax on the income; there is just no form. Thresholds change, so check the current one.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.body: You earn $1,640 in a quarter. A 25% set-aside is $410.

blocks.title: A simple monthly habit
blocks.body: On the 1st of each month, move 25% of last month's cleared earnings into a separate savings pot. In a $400 month that is $100. Adjust the percentage with a tax professional.

blocks.title: Set money aside as you go
blocks.body: Many creators set aside 25 to 30 percent of earnings. Ask a tax professional what is right for you, and keep receipts for what you spend on the work.

blocks.title: Gifts are taxable too
blocks.body: Free products or perks can count as income. The Tax Desk only sees what flowd pays you, so keep your own record of anything else.

blocks.title: Your Tax Desk
blocks.body:
Submit the W-9 (US) or W-8BEN (outside the US)
Watch year-to-date cleared and paid
See your progress toward the $2,000 1099-NEC line
Export a CSV for your accountant

quiz.prompt: When does flowd ask for a W-9?
options: At your first approval, before your first payout
quiz.explanation: Just-in-time: we ask when it matters.

quiz.prompt: A 1099-NEC is issued at what amount (2026 payments)?
quiz.explanation: The threshold for 2026 payments is $2,000.

quiz.prompt: Is this tax advice?
quiz.explanation: flowd gives general information only.

title: Spotting scams
summary: The five patterns and how Scam Shield helps.

blocks.body: Scams in creator marketplaces are repetitive. Once you know the patterns they stop working.

blocks.title: The five patterns
blocks.body:
They ask you to pay
They want to move to another app
The brand is not verified
The bounty is not Funded
The link goes somewhere strange

blocks.title: Why people fall for them
blocks.body: Scams borrow urgency and flattery: "we love your content", "only three slots left", "confirm in the next hour". A real bounty does not need a decision in an hour. The quickest check is not about how the message feels but about where the money is and where the conversation is happening.

blocks.title: Anatomy of a scam message
blocks.body: "Hi! We love your content. We pay $400 per video. First, move to Telegram and buy a $50 gift card to verify your account." Three flags in three sentences: off-platform, money out, urgency.

blocks.title: Verify a brand in 30 seconds
blocks.body:
Verified badge on the brand
Funded badge on the bounty
Scorecard shows real decisions
Chat stays in flowd

blocks.title: What flowd does for you
blocks.body: Scam Shield warns on risky messages inside the chat, blocks briefs that demand a burner account, and keeps unfunded bounties from going live. Every report gets a case number and a human first look within 24 hours.

blocks.title: Look for the Funded badge
blocks.body: If a bounty is not Funded, the money is not in escrow. Do not start work until it is.

blocks.title: Report it
blocks.body: Tap Report on any bounty, message or brand. A human reads every report and replies within 24 hours.

blocks.title: If you already paid
blocks.body: Stop sending money, tell your bank or payment app, change any password you shared, and report it in the app with screenshots. Never send more money to "recover" the first payment.

quiz.prompt: What does the Funded badge mean?
options: The full budget is in escrow
quiz.explanation: Funded = the full budget and fee reserve are escrowed.

quiz.prompt: A "brand" asks for gift cards. You...
quiz.explanation: Never pay to work.

quiz.prompt: Where should chat happen?
quiz.explanation: In-app chat is protected by Scam Shield.

title: Rate cards and negotiating
summary: Set a price that fits your audience, with paid usage priced up front.

blocks.body: From Silver tier you can publish a rate card: your price per video, your minimum CPM and what paid usage costs. Brands can buy directly at your ask.

blocks.title: Setting your price
blocks.body:
Look at the market-suggested band
Start near the middle for your tier
Price paid usage separately
Set a turnaround
Choose your availability

blocks.title: Where the suggested price comes from
blocks.body: The band uses your median views over 28 days, the clearing CPM of the app category and a multiplier for paid usage. It shows a low, a middle and a high price with a confidence label, because small samples are noisy. It is a starting point, not a rule, and it moves as the market does.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.body: Median 14k views at about $2.10 per 1,000 views is roughly $29 from a pool bounty. A dedicated video also prices your time and your usage rights, so the market-suggested band for that reach is higher, around $80 to $115. A rate card at $140 for one video with 90 days of paid usage is a fair ask for Silver, and it leaves room to counter.

blocks.title: Pricing a bundle
blocks.body: One dedicated video with 90 days of paid usage: $180. Three videos: $150 each ($450). Paid-usage renewal: $45 per extra 30 days. Turnaround: 5 days. A bundle discount signals confidence without lowering your single-video price.

blocks.title: Countering well
blocks.body: You can counter an offer up to three rounds, and every message stays in the app. A good counter names what changes: price, usage term, turnaround or number of videos. "I can do $140 if usage is 30 days instead of 90" is easier to accept than a bare number, and the brand sees the all-in price with the fee on every round.

blocks.title: Use the suggestion
blocks.body: The market-suggested price shows the range for creators like you. Sit near the middle until you have two or three settled bounties of your own to point at.

blocks.title: Counter, do not give in
blocks.body: Know your minimum before you start. If the brand cannot meet it, a polite decline costs nothing and leaves the door open for the next offer.

quiz.prompt: From which tier can you have a rate card?
quiz.explanation: Rate cards unlock at Silver.

quiz.prompt: How many counter rounds are allowed?
quiz.explanation: A maximum of three counter rounds keeps negotiations short.

quiz.prompt: Paid usage should be...
quiz.explanation: Price paid usage up front.

title: Reading analytics and retention curves
summary: What the retention curve and the funnel tell you about your next video.

blocks.body: Every post has a retention curve: the share of viewers still watching at each point. The steepest drop is the part to fix.

blocks.title: How to read it
blocks.body:
Look for the first drop (usually the hook)
Look at the middle (the demo)
Look at the end (the call to action)
Compare with your last three posts

blocks.title: The funnel under the views
blocks.body: Views are the top of a funnel: views, link clicks, installs, trials, paid. Conversions through your link and code are Tracked; modelled and survey numbers are Estimated and never add to your pay. A post with 8,000 views and 30 tracked installs is doing more for the brand than a post with 40,000 views and none.

blocks.title: Reading a retention curve
blocks.body: Views 20,400. Retention: 100% at 0s, 52% at 1s, 41% at 3s, then a flat 38% to the end. The hook lost half the audience; the body held the rest. Rewrite the first line, keep the body.

blocks.title: What the scores are
blocks.body: The Hook Score and Flow Score are checklist scores. They check things that tend to matter: hook timing, the app on screen, beats, disclosure. They do not predict results, and they get sharper as bounties settle and flowd learns which checklist items really moved trials. Treat a low score as a fix list, not a verdict.

blocks.title: Fix the first drop
blocks.body: Most improvement comes from the first 3 seconds. Rewrite the hook, not the whole video.

blocks.title: Views are not outcomes
blocks.body: A post with fewer views can drive more trials. Check the funnel: views, clicks, installs, trials, paid.

blocks.title: Your weekly 10 minutes
blocks.body:
Pick your two best and two worst posts
Compare the first 3 seconds
Compare trial rate per install, not just views
Write one change for next week

quiz.prompt: Where is the retention drop usually biggest?
quiz.explanation: The hook decides who stays.

quiz.prompt: Fewer views always means a worse post.
quiz.explanation: Trial rate per install can be higher on a smaller post.

quiz.prompt: What should you fix first?
quiz.explanation: The hook is the highest-leverage fix.

title: Sustainable cadence and burnout
summary: Weekly streaks, freezes, rest weeks and a pace that you can keep.

blocks.body: The best creators keep a pace they can sustain. Streaks here are weekly, forgiving and never guilt you.

blocks.title: How streaks work
blocks.body:
Post at least once in an ISO week to count
Earn one freeze for every 4-week streak (max 2 banked)
Declare up to 2 rest weeks per quarter
Missing a week without a freeze simply ends the streak; nothing is lost

blocks.title: Pick a baseline, not a maximum
blocks.body: Count the posts you can make in your worst week and make that your target. For most people it is one. Everything above the baseline is a bonus week, not a new standard, and a streak only ever asks for one post per ISO week.

blocks.title: A pace that survives a bad week
blocks.body: Plan two posts a week, ship one on a good week, bank a freeze on every fourth week, and declare a rest week before a trip. Your streak, your tier and your reliability score are unaffected by a rest week.

blocks.title: Money and rest are separate
blocks.body: Pay never depends on your streak: a bounty pays the same whether you are on week 1 or week 12. Your tier does not drop for 30 days after a dip, there is no inactivity penalty, and nothing is lost when a streak ends.

blocks.title: When you are running on empty
blocks.body:
Turn on Wellbeing Mode quiet hours
Use a banked freeze or declare a rest week
Pause up to 90 days if you need it
Tier and streak stay exactly as they are

blocks.title: Use Wellbeing Mode
blocks.body: Quiet hours, numbers-off and Pause keep your tier and your streak safe while you rest.

blocks.title: Burnout is real
blocks.body: If it stops being fun, take a rest week. Your tier does not drop for 30 days after a dip.

quiz.prompt: A streak week counts when you...
options: Post at least once in the ISO week
quiz.explanation: One post per week is enough.

quiz.prompt: How many freezes can you bank?
quiz.explanation: Max 2 banked; you earn one per 4-week streak.

quiz.prompt: Does your tier drop right away after a dip?
quiz.explanation: No tier drop for 30 days after a dip.
